subject: Banking
title: The Inflation Mistake of 2021
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Inflation Mistake of 2021.

hook.text: In 2021, the Fed called inflation 'transitory' and kept rates at zero. It lasted 18 months and peaked at 9.1%.

buildup.text: Pandemic stimulus checks, supply chain disruptions, and low rates fueled spending.

discovery.text: The Fed delayed rate hikes by months, believing inflation would fade. By the time they acted, it had become entrenched.

twist.text: The delay forced the fastest rate hikes in 40 years. A gradual adjustment became an emergency response.

climax.text: Calling inflation transitory was the Fed's biggest recent mistake.

punchline.text: Called it transitory. Waited too long. Then raised rates at record speed.

quiz.question: What did the Fed call inflation in 2021?

details.summary: The Fed dismissed 2021 inflation as transitory, maintaining near-zero rates and bond purchases as prices surged. When inflation proved persistent, the delayed response required the most aggressive rate hikes in forty years.
details.whyItMatters: The transitory inflation call was the Fed's biggest policy error in decades. It eroded central bank credibility and forced painful catch-up rate increases that risked recession and destabilized banking.
takeaways: The Fed kept rates near zero while inflation exceeded 7 percent
Transitory became the most mocked word in economics by late 2021
The delayed response required raising rates from near zero to over 5 percent

faq.question: Why did the Fed believe inflation was transitory?
faq.answer: The Fed expected pandemic supply chain disruptions to resolve quickly. Historical models suggested supply-driven inflation would fade on its own. Massive fiscal stimulus and accumulated consumer savings added demand pressures the models missed.

faq.question: What were the consequences of the transitory mistake?
faq.answer: Inflation peaked at 9.1% in June 2022. The Fed raised rates at the fastest pace since the 1980s, from near zero to over 5%. The rapid tightening contributed to the 2023 bank failures as bond portfolios lost billions in value.
